clue.text: Tries again at rear of mule train

parts.note: a court that tries a case again rehears it

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of mule is taken

explanation.surface: Someone retries a stubborn mule at the back of a pack train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like part of the mule train scene; it is the definition, in the sense of practise.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a performance before giving it is to prepare or train for it.

clue.text: Set right about frock

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: Someone adjusts a frock that sits wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right a wrong or an imbalance is a synonym of the verb set right.

clue.text: Search round a place frequently visited

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, so the letter A sits within the word for search

parts.note: to search for something is to hunt

explanation.surface: Hunting all round a popular spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite spot that someone keeps returning to is their regular stamping ground.

clue.text: Conservative blocking amendment causes heated dispute

indicators.note: a piece that is blocking a word stands in its way, inside it

parts.note: an amendment is an alteration

explanation.surface: A Tory obstructing a parliamentary amendment sparks a furious row.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry argument or quarrel is a noisy dispute.

clue.text: Toboggan beginning to slide over projecting shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next
the beginning of a word is its first letter, here that of slide

parts.note: a ledge is a shelf that juts out

explanation.surface: A toboggan starts to slide off the edge of a jutting rock shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A small vehicle on runners for sliding down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Animal in forest, a gazelle

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words forest, a gazelle, running across the comma

explanation.surface: A gazelle spotted among the trees of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' could seem to go with gazelle; the answer runs across forest and a.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult male deer is an animal, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Come about act available

parts.note: a turn is an act in a variety show
a book that is out has been published and is available

explanation.surface: A stage turn becomes available when a slot comes free.
explanation.definitionFit: To come about is to happen or prove to be the case in the end, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Good to wander in small wooded area

parts.note: to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: It is pleasant to stroll in a little wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wood or group of trees, often planted, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Be suspicious of party, but relaxed.

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters of but come loose and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of a party yet feels at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrust or question someone's honesty, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Briefly board ship prior to travel ban

indicators.note: prior to places the first piece before the next
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word for board ship goes

parts.note: to embark is to board a ship
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A quick boarding before a travel ban takes effect.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition on trade or movement is a ban.

clue.text: A dark horse in the field of children's literature

definitions.text: A dark horse in the field of children's literature

parts.words: A dark horse in the field of children's literature
parts.note: a dark horse is usually an unexpected contender, but here it is literally a black horse, the title character of Anna Sewell's classic novel

explanation.surface: An unexpected contender emerges among writers for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' and 'field' read as racing or contest idioms; in fact the horse is literally black and lives in a famous book.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Sewell's 1877 novel, a staple of young readers' shelves, is narrated by a black horse.

clue.text: Have a meal, warm, without husband

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for husband is removed

parts.note: to warm something is to heat it

explanation.surface: Someone eats a warm dinner alone, the husband absent.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine or consume food, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Doctor and MA having part in complex procedure

parts.note: to doctor results is to falsify or rig them
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A physician and a Master of Arts take part in an elaborate procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun beside MA; it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, tiresome and complicated process or set of formalities.

clue.text: Colas I ordered for party

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone orders soft drinks for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like buying drinks; it rearranges COLASI.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering or party, a noun use of the word.

clue.text: Business worry

definitions.meaning: a going ... is a firm or company

explanation.definitionFit: A firm can be called a going concern, and the same word means anxiety.

clue.text: Drawing of small sailing vessel

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A drawing of a little sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'small sailing vessel' as one picture; 'small' is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough or quick drawing is a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Cheer that woman catching a number

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the letter A is held inside the word for that woman

parts.note: her refers to that woman
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A woman gives a cheer on catching a number in a lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching' puts A inside HER to make HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to encourage or embolden them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Save about a litre in cask

parts.note: save means except, as does bar (all bar one)
re means about or concerning
L is the abbreviation for a litre

explanation.surface: Someone keeps roughly a litre in a wooden cask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like keep; it means except, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel is a wooden vessel with bulging sides for holding liquid, the same as a cask.

clue.text: Justify being very mean

parts.note: to mean something is to indicate it

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their very stingy behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy; it is the verb, signify.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something to be right or reasonable, clearing it of doubt, is to justify it.

clue.text: Member of the clergy visiting Civic Arena

indicators.note: visiting means staying a while within, so the letters stay inside the words Civic Arena

explanation.surface: A clergyman pays a visit to the town's civic arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Cut fruit, then vegetable

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter of the fruit is lopped off

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Slice some fruit, then a vegetable, for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The round green seed eaten as a vegetable, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Bother with duck sauce

parts.note: a pest is a bother or nuisance
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Is it worth the bother of making a sauce to go with duck?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird served with sauce; it is a cricket score of zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A green Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and cheese.

clue.text: Daily in circulation, originally thinner

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of circulation is taken

parts.note: leaner means thinner

explanation.surface: A daily newspaper in circulation that has grown thinner than it used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests a newspaper; in British usage a daily is a domestic help who comes in each day to clean.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a daily is a housekeeper or charwoman who comes in every day.

clue.text: Leading group capsized

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, leading
a set is a group

explanation.surface: The front-running crew's boat overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that has overturned is described as tipped over.

clue.text: Draw a circle round item of jewellery

definitions.meaning: to encircle something with a pen mark
a band worn on the finger

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means encircle with a mark; the noun is a band worn on a finger.

clue.text: Make light of losing on stage show

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so this piece follows the next

parts.note: a play is a stage show
a team that is down is behind, losing

explanation.surface: A theatre show making light of its losses.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise or understate the importance of something, a phrasal-verb synonym.
